text:
anya: Repro'd on staging with INT8-KV enabled. Memory win is real (~30% less memory on 32k context) but we see decode divergence after ~1.2k tokens for a subset of prompts. Opening thread to collect quick repros and decide mitigation. TL;DR: int8 KV = good perf/mem but intermittent quality drift on long prefixes.

kai: Which model/config and the exact repro steps?

anya: model=redwood/open-7b-v2, runtime=v2.4.1, kv_quant=int8, kernel_policy=auto, batcher=dynamic (batch window 20ms in the repro below). Repro steps:
```
# repro (staging container)
export RW_MODEL=redwood/open-7b-v2
export RW_RUNTIME=v2.4.1
# enable int8 kv cache
./serve --model $RW_MODEL --kv-quant int8 --kernel-policy auto --batch-window-ms 20 &
# fire a long-context generation (32k prefix trimmed in this example)
curl -s -X POST localhost:8080/v1/generate -d '{"prompt": "<~32k prefix...> \nQ: Explain the asymptotic behavior of ...","max_tokens": 2000}' > out.json
```

anya: Sample mismatch (FP16 vs INT8-KV):
FP16 decode (correct): "...and therefore the algorithm converges to the fixed point with rate O(1/n)."
INT8-KV decode (diverged): "...and so we see oscillations that do not settle, giving an incorrect limit behaviour."
(Shortened for thread)

perf-bot: CI run 1841234490 results attached: int8-kv p50 token latency 3.1ms (-18% vs fp16), p95 9.6ms (-12%), memory resident 18.2GB vs 26.5GB FP16. However eval on extended-context evalset shows average match_score drop ~0.07 absolute (quality regression).

matt: My hunch: kernel selection path is flipping between int8 and fp16 at certain seq_len thresholds which can change numeric ordering and LN scaling -> jitter accumulates. Check kernel logs for fallback points and quant scale drift.

anya: grabbing runtime logs now, snippets: 
```
[2026-06-02T14:12:01Z] kernel_select: chosen=int8_gemm_v2 fallback=fp16_conv when seq_len>2048
[2026-06-02T14:12:01Z] kv_cache: quant_scale=0.0034 zero_point=127
[2026-06-02T14:12:01Z] batching: dynamic_window_ms=20 avg_batch=12
```

sandra: Quick experiment idea: force deterministic kernel for decode only to fp16 and keep int8 for cache storage. env RW_FORCE_KERNEL=fp16_decode or set kernel_policy to hybrid with decode=fp16, kv=int8. If drift disappears we pin the auto policy until calibration fixes it.

anya: ran forced fp16_decode on same staging host: divergence goes away. Numbers: p50 token latency rises to 3.9ms, p95 11.2ms, memory goes up to ~22GB (still better than full fp16), quality returns to baseline.

jeff: Proposed immediate plan: 1) revert kernel_policy=auto for long-context customers to hybrid (kv=int8, decode=fp16) via a rollout flag; 2) add canary tests for long prefixes in CI; 3) follow-up PR to improve quant calibration (scale per-layer/time) and deterministic kernel selection heuristics. Can someone open the issue and a PR for the revert?

anya: opened issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/4123 (int8-kv long-context decode drift) and started a small PR to add a hybrid kernel policy toggle: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4157 (WIP).

matt: For the calibration work I'll add a micro-benchmark that forces long-prefix step-throughs and logs per-layer quant_scale over time. If we see scale drift correlated with divergence we'll try per-step re-scaling or stored FP32 scales in KV metadata as an experiment.

kai: For the rollback, can we gate by model family and seq_len>8k? i.e., only enable hybrid for >8k contexts so most customers keep auto/int8 wins.

jeff: yes, gate + telemetry. also add a short eval job that runs a few prompt families with 16k+ prefixes on every release branch.

anya: I'll coordinate the canary rollout and add our minimal repro to the issue. Thanks all, will post updates in this thread when PR lands. :thumbsup:
